proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an arbitrary enumeration \(\mathcal S=(s_1,\ldots,s_k)\), and write \(q_a=\Pi_{s_a}\), \(D_a=D_{s_a}\), and \(\overline D=\sum_aq_aD_a=M(\Pi)\).  The probability law gives \(\sum_aq_a=1\).  For matrices \(X_a\) of a common dimension and \(\overline X=\sum_aq_aX_a\), direct expansion gives
\[
 \sum_aq_a(X_a-\overline X)^{\top}J(X_a-\overline X)
 =\sum_aq_aX_a^{\top}JX_a-\overline X^{\top}J\overline X
 =\frac12\sum_{a,b}q_aq_b(X_a-X_b)^{\top}J(X_a-X_b).
\]
Taking \(X_a=D_a\), deleting the diagonal terms, and pairing \((a,b)\) with \((b,a)\) yields
\[
 G(\Pi)
 =\frac1T\sum_{a<b}q_aq_b(D_a-D_b)^{\top}J(D_a-D_b)
 =\sum_{a<b}q_aq_bB_{ab}.
\]

For fixed \((t,\ell)\), put \(x_a=(D_a)_{t,\ell}\).  Expanding both sides of the finite cross-covariance identity gives
\[
 \sum_aq_a(D_a-\overline D)^{\top}Je_tx_a
 =\sum_aq_aD_a^{\top}Je_tx_a
  -\overline D^{\top}Je_t\sum_aq_ax_a
 =\sum_{a<b}q_aq_b(D_a-D_b)^{\top}Je_t(x_a-x_b).
\]
Since \(R_{s_a}=J(D_a-\overline D)\) and \(x_a-x_b=(E_{ab})_{t,\ell}\), division by \(T\) proves
\[
 h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)=\sum_{a<b}q_aq_bb_{ab,t,\ell}.
\]

The matrix \(J\) is symmetric and idempotent.  Thus
\[
 v^{\top}B_{ab}v
 =T^{-1}(E_{ab}v)^{\top}J(E_{ab}v)
 =T^{-1}\|JE_{ab}v\|_2^2.
\]
The floor assumption gives \(q_aq_b\geq\epsilon^2>0\).  Therefore
\[
 v^{\top}G(\Pi)v=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 JE_{ab}v=0\text{ for every }a<b.
\]
The same sum of squares without weights gives
\[
 v^{\top}H_{\mathcal S}v=T^{-1}\sum_{a<b}\|JE_{ab}v\|_2^2.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \ker G(\Pi)=\bigcap_{a<b}\ker(JE_{ab})=\ker H_{\mathcal S}.
\]
The right-hand side depends only on the listed support, so nonsingularity for one positive law is equivalent to nonsingularity for every positive law on that support.  No absorption property was used.

Path overlap gives \(\pi_s(X)\geq c_{\pi}>0\), so the inverse propensities in \(\theta(\Pi)\) are well defined.  Conditional on \(X\), consistency and conditional pathwise mean random assignment give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\left.\frac{\Pi_W}{\pi_W(X)}A_W(\Pi)Y\right|X\right]
 &=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\pi_s(X)\frac{\Pi_s}{\pi_s(X)}A_s(\Pi)
   \mathbb E_P[Y\mid W=s,X]\\
 &=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\Pi_sA_s(\Pi)\mu(s,X).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Let \(m(X)=(m_1(X),\ldots,m_T(X))^{\top}\).  The calendar-memory condition is
\[
 \mu(s,X)=m(X)+\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{\ell=0}^p
 e_t\tau_{t,\ell}(X)(D_s)_{t,\ell}.
\]
Since \(M(\Pi)=\sum_s\Pi_sD_s\),
\[
 \sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)=J\left(\sum_s\Pi_sD_s-M(\Pi)\right)=0.
\]
It follows that the unrestricted baseline cancels:
\[
 \sum_s\Pi_sA_s(\Pi)m(X)
 =T^{-1}G(\Pi)^{-1}\left(\sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)^{\top}\right)m(X)=0.
\]
For each effect cell,
\[
 \sum_s\Pi_sA_s(\Pi)e_t(D_s)_{t,\ell}
 =G(\Pi)^{-1}\left\{T^{-1}\sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)^{\top}e_t(D_s)_{t,\ell}\right\}
 =L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi).
\]
Taking expectation over \(X\), interchanging only finite sums, and using \(\tau_{t,\ell}=\mathbb E_P[\tau_{t,\ell}(X)]\) proves the causal loading representation.  The inverse exists by \(G(\Pi)\succ0\).

For the design identities, let \(W^{\Pi}\sim\Pi\), extend its coordinates by zero outside the panel, and note
\[
 M(\Pi)_{t,j}=\mathbb E_{\Pi}[W^{\Pi}_{t-j}],
 \qquad
 C_{\Pi}(u,v)=\operatorname{Cov}_{\Pi}(W^{\Pi}_u,W^{\Pi}_v).
\]
Using \(J_{uv}=\mathbf 1\{u=v\}-T^{-1}\) and expanding the definition of \(G\) coordinatewise gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 G_{jr}(\Pi)
 &=T^{-1}\sum_{u=1}^T\sum_{v=1}^TJ_{uv}
   C_{\Pi}(u-j,v-r)\\
 &=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^TC_{\Pi}(t-j,t-r)
   -T^{-2}\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{v=1}^TC_{\Pi}(t-j,v-r).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Likewise,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 h_{t,\ell,j}(\Pi)
 &=T^{-1}\sum_{v=1}^TJ_{vt}C_{\Pi}(v-j,t-\ell)\\
 &=T^{-1}\left\{C_{\Pi}(t-j,t-\ell)
  -T^{-1}\sum_{v=1}^TC_{\Pi}(v-j,t-\ell)\right\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
These calculations use no ordering or absorption.

If \(\mathcal S\) is absorbing, then for \(u\leq T\),
\[
 W^{\Pi}_u=\mathbf 1\{a(W^{\Pi})\leq u\}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 C_{\Pi}(u,v)
 =F_{\Pi}(\min\{u,v\})-F_{\Pi}(u)F_{\Pi}(v)
 =K_{\Pi}(u,v),
\]
including nonpositive boundary indices because both variables and \(F_{\Pi}\) are then zero.  This proves the ordered Green corollary.

Finally, with \(e_{\ell}\in\mathbb R^d\) denoting the lag-coordinate vector,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{t=1}^Th_{t,\ell}(\Pi)
 &=T^{-1}\sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)^{\top}D_se_{\ell}\\
 &=T^{-1}\sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)^{\top}\{D_s-M(\Pi)\}e_{\ell}\\
 &=T^{-1}\sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)^{\top}R_s(\Pi)e_{\ell}
 =G(\Pi)e_{\ell}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The second equality uses \(\sum_s\Pi_sR_s=0\); the third uses \(R_s=J(D_s-M)\), symmetry, and idempotence of \(J\).  Multiplication by \(G(\Pi)^{-1}\) gives
\[
 \sum_{t=1}^TL_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)=e_j^{\top}e_{\ell}=\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}.
\]

Under the stated calendar-homogeneity restriction, write the common effect at lag \(\ell\) as \(\overline\tau_{\ell}\).  The causal loading representation and normalization give
\[
 \theta_j(\Pi)
 =\sum_{\ell=0}^p\sum_{t=1}^TL_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)\overline\tau_{\ell}
 =\sum_{\ell=0}^p\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}\overline\tau_{\ell}
 =\overline\tau_j.
\]
This argument uses only the present superpopulation assumptions; no inclusion relation with a different sampling class is invoked.

For strictness, take the support and law in the statement.  The lag designs, their mean, and the time residualizer are
\[
 D_{000}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
 D_{001}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
 D_{011}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
 M=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1/3&0\\2/3&1/3\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
 J=\begin{pmatrix}2/3&-1/3&-1/3\\-1/3&2/3&-1/3\\-1/3&-1/3&2/3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Direct substitution into the definitions gives
\[
 G=\begin{pmatrix}2/27&0\\0&4/81\end{pmatrix},
\]
and the only nonzero numerator vectors are
\[
 h_{2,0}=\begin{pmatrix}1/27\\-2/81\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 h_{3,0}=\begin{pmatrix}1/27\\2/81\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 h_{3,1}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\4/81\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Since \(G^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(27/2,81/4)\), the corresponding loadings are
\[
 L_{\cdot,2,0}=\begin{pmatrix}1/2\\-1/2\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 L_{\cdot,3,0}=\begin{pmatrix}1/2\\1/2\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 L_{\cdot,3,1}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The loading theorem therefore gives exactly the two coefficient formulas in the statement.  Holding \(\tau_{3,1}\) fixed while varying \(\tau_{2,0}\) and \(\tau_{3,0}\) separately changes \(\theta_1\); hence no time-homogeneous lag-effect vector determines the coefficient outside the homogeneous submodel.

To embed the witness in the published sampling conditions, take units independent, draw each \(W_i\) from the displayed three-point law independently of its full potential-outcome schedule, and choose deterministic bounded schedules obeying the displayed mean model.  Then maximal correlations vanish for \(i\neq j\), the three propensities equal \(1/3\), second moments are bounded, and the computed \(G\) is positive definite.  Thus the same algebraic nonreduction occurs in that sampling setup when calendar variation is admitted.

Every listed path is binary, so every \(D_s\) and \(E_{ab}\) has integer entries, while \(J=I_T-\mathbf 1_T\mathbf 1_T^{\top}/T\) has rational entries.  Hence \(B_{ab}\), \(b_{ab,t,\ell}\), and \(H_{\mathcal S}\) are rational objects obtained by finitely many rational operations, without any absorption requirement.

Perform exact Gaussian elimination over \(\mathbb Q\) on the \(d\)-by-\(d\) matrix \(H_{\mathcal S}\).  If it is singular, elimination terminates with a nonzero \(v\in\mathbb Q^d\) satisfying \(H_{\mathcal S}v=0\).  The sum-of-squares identity from \(\mathrm{lem{:}support\text{-}rank}\) gives
\[
 0=v^{\top}H_{\mathcal S}v
 =T^{-1}\sum_{a<b}\|JE_{ab}v\|_2^2,
\]
so \(JE_{ab}v=0\) for every pair.  This is an exact singularity certificate.

If \(H_{\mathcal S}\) is nonsingular, the support-rank lemma and \(\Pi_s\geq\epsilon>0\) imply that \(G(\Pi)\) is nonsingular.  Rationality of \(\Pi\) and the pair identities imply that every entry of \(G(\Pi)\) and every \(h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)\) is rational.  Exact elimination therefore computes \(G(\Pi)^{-1}\) and all entries of
\[
 L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi)=G(\Pi)^{-1}h_{t,\ell}(\Pi).
\]
Rationality of \(\omega\) makes \(Q\) rational.  For each of the finitely many triples \((j,t,\ell)\), exact comparison of \(L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)-Q_{j,t,\ell}\) with zero returns its sign, including equality.  Summing the exact rational absolute values returns \(\mathcal C(\Pi,Q)\).  Both branches use finite-dimensional exact Gaussian elimination and finitely many rational comparisons, so they terminate with the asserted output.

Because an absorbing binary path is determined by its adoption date, distinct supported paths have distinct dates and can be ordered strictly.  For \(a<b\), every \(r\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\), and \(j\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\),
\[
 (E_{ab})_{r,j}
 =\mathbf 1\{u_a\leq r-j\}-\mathbf 1\{u_b\leq r-j\}
 =\mathbf 1\{u_a\leq r-j<u_b\}
 =(I_{ab})_{r,j}.
\]
This equality includes nonpositive shifted indices and the never-treated endpoint \(T+1\), because the relevant indicators then vanish as specified.

Positivity makes every adjacent ratio well defined.  Recursion and normalization give
\[
 \frac{\Pi_{s_a}}{\Pi_{s_1}}=\prod_{r=1}^{a-1}\rho_r=z_a,
 \qquad
 \Pi_{s_a}=\frac{z_a}{Z}.
\]
Substitution of \(E_{ab}=I_{ab}\) and \(\Pi_{s_a}\Pi_{s_b}=z_az_b/Z^2\) into the pair-mass identities yields
\[
 G(\Pi)=Z^{-2}\Gamma(\rho),
 \qquad
 h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)=Z^{-2}g_{t,\ell}(\rho).
\]
The assumed support rank, equivalently the graph connectivity criterion of \(\mathrm{lem{:}absorbing\text{-}graph\text{-}rank}\), and positivity imply \(G(\Pi)\succ0\).  Hence \(\Gamma(\rho)=Z^2G(\Pi)\succ0\), so \(\det\Gamma(\rho)>0\), and the common scale cancels:
\[
 L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi)=\Gamma(\rho)^{-1}g_{t,\ell}(\rho).
\]

For an invertible matrix, the cofactor expansion gives \(\Gamma\operatorname{adj}(\Gamma)=\det(\Gamma)I_d\).  Expanding the determinant after replacing column \(j\) by \(g_{t,\ell}\) gives
\[
 e_j^{\top}\operatorname{adj}(\Gamma)g_{t,\ell}=\Delta_{j,t,\ell}(\rho).
\]
Therefore
\[
 L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)
 =\frac{e_j^{\top}\operatorname{adj}(\Gamma)g_{t,\ell}}{\det\Gamma}
 =\frac{\Delta_{j,t,\ell}(\rho)}{\det\Gamma(\rho)}.
\]
The denominator is strictly positive, proving the pointwise sign and zero equivalences.  Their finite conjunction over \(j\neq\ell\) is precisely the stated off-diagonal certificate.

Finally, \(\Pi_{s_a}=z_a/Z\) proves \(\Pi_{s_a}\geq\epsilon\Longleftrightarrow z_a\geq\epsilon Z\).  Every entry of \(I_{ab}\) is fixed by the integer endpoints, and every \(z_a\) is a monomial in the adjacent ratios.  Thus \(\Gamma\), \(g\), and all replacement-column determinants have rational entries when the ratios are rational.  Exact determinant evaluation and rational sign comparison terminate.  Repeated shifted coordinates or out-of-panel arguments merely repeat or zero entries of the interval matrices, so no additional inversion is used.  The proof evaluates one specified \(\rho\); it supplies no assertion about how the determinant hypersurfaces partition the full continuous feasible ratio region.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal S\) is absorbing, and write its distinct adoption dates as \(u_a=a(s_a)\).  Form the undirected graph \(\mathfrak G_{\mathcal S}\) with vertex set \(\{\bot,0,\ldots,p\}\) as follows.  For every \(a<b\) and \(t\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\), join \(t-u_a\) to \(t-u_b\) if both indices belong to \(\{0,\ldots,p\}\), and join the unique in-range index to \(\bot\) if exactly one belongs to \(\{0,\ldots,p\}\).  Then
\[
 \dim\ker G(\Pi)
 =\#\{\text{connected components of }\mathfrak G_{\mathcal S}\text{ not containing }\bot\}.
\]
Thus \(G(\Pi)\) has full rank for every positive law on \(\mathcal S\) if and only if every lag vertex \(0,\ldots,p\) is connected to \(\bot\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(v=(v_0,\ldots,v_p)^{\top}\in\mathbb R^d\), and extend it by \(\widetilde v_j=v_j\) for \(0\leq j\leq p\) and \(\widetilde v_j=0\) otherwise.  For \(a<b\), absorption gives
\[
 (E_{ab})_{t,j}
 =\mathbf 1\{u_a\leq t-j<u_b\}.
\]
Put \(x^{ab}=E_{ab}v\).  Since \(J\) is the orthogonal projector onto the vectors perpendicular to \(\mathbf 1_T\),
\[
 JE_{ab}v=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 x^{ab}_1=\cdots=x^{ab}_T
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 x^{ab}_t-x^{ab}_{t-1}=0\quad(2\leq t\leq T).
\]
The boundary convention and the displayed interval formula yield, term by term,
\[
 x^{ab}_t-x^{ab}_{t-1}
 =\sum_{j=0}^pv_j
 \left(\mathbf 1\{t-j=u_a\}-\mathbf 1\{t-j=u_b\}\right)
 =\widetilde v_{t-u_a}-\widetilde v_{t-u_b}.
\]
Hence \(JE_{ab}v=0\) for every pair exactly when the values attached to the two in-range vertices are equal for every graph edge and the value at every vertex joined to \(\bot\) is zero, where \(\bot\) carries the fixed value zero.  It follows that a solution is constant on each connected component, its constant is forced to zero on the component containing \(\bot\), and the constants on all other components are free and independent.  The solution space therefore has dimension equal to the number of components not containing \(\bot\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}support\text{-}rank}\), this solution space is \(\ker G(\Pi)\) for every positive \(\Pi\).  The full-rank criterion follows because the graph has precisely the \(d=p+1\) lag vertices in addition to \(\bot\).
added_lemmas.justification: The graph converts the support-only matrix kernel into a complete combinatorial full-rank test for absorbing supports.
added_lemmas.gap: The published dynamic RIPW rank condition is algebraic and does not classify rank from ordered adoption endpoints.
added_lemmas.consumer: The public \(\texttt{ripw}\) workflow can certify rank by finite graph connectivity before computing any reshaping probabilities.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(T\) and \(p\) be fixed.  Let \(\mathcal S\subseteq\{0,1\}^{T}\) be finite, contain at least two paths and at least one path outside \(\{0_T,1_T\}\), and let \(\Pi_s>0\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\), with \(\sum_s\Pi_s=1\) and \(G(\Pi)\succ0\).  For each \(n\), consider unit-indexed observed paths \((W_i,Y_i)\) and full potential-outcome schedules \(\mathcal Y_i=\{Y_{it}(w):t\in\{1,\ldots,T\},\ w\in\{0,1\}^{T}\}\), with \(Y_i=Y_i(W_i)\).  Suppose: (i) the maximal correlations \(\rho_{ij}\) between the sigma-fields generated by \((\mathcal Y_i,W_i)\) and \((\mathcal Y_j,W_j)\) satisfy \(n^{-2}\sum_{i,j=1}^n\rho_{ij}=O(n^{-q})\) for some fixed \(q\in(0,1]\); (ii) the known generalized propensity \(\pi_i(w)=\mathbb P(W_i=w\mid\mathcal Y_i)\) satisfies \(\pi_i(s)\geq c_{\pi}>0\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\); (iii) \(\sup_{n,i,t,w}\mathbb E[Y_{it}(w)^2]<\infty\); and (iv), for every \(i,t,w\),
\[
 \mathbb E[Y_{it}(w)]=\mu_{it}+\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}\tau_{i,t,\ell}w_{t-\ell},
 \qquad w_{u}=0\text{ for }u\leq0.
\]
Define \(\overline\tau_{t,\ell,n}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\tau_{i,t,\ell}\).  Then the published-setup RIPW coefficient satisfies
\[
 \widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ex},n}
 -\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}
 L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi)\overline\tau_{t,\ell,n}
 =o_P(1).
\]
If \(\tau_{i,t,\ell}=\tau_{i,\ell}\) for every \(i,t,\ell\), then
\[
 \widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ex},n,j}
 =\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\tau_{i,j}+o_P(1),
 \qquad j\in\{0,\ldots,p\},
\]
which is the coefficient conclusion of Theorem \(4.1\) of Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo under their unit-indexed known-propensity sampling conditions.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(\Theta_i=\Pi_{W_i}/\pi_i(W_i)\), with \(\Pi_w=0\) for \(w\notin\mathcal S\).  Assumption (ii) gives \(0\leq\Theta_i\leq c_{\pi}^{-1}\).  Conditional on \(\mathcal Y_i\), inverse-propensity cancellation gives, for every integrable function \(f\),
\[
 \mathbb E[\Theta_i f(W_i,Y_i(W_i))\mid\mathcal Y_i]
 =\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\Pi_s f(s,Y_i(s)).
\]
In particular,
\[
 \mathbb E\Theta_i=1,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[\Theta_iD_{W_i}]=M(\Pi).
\]

We first record the weak-dependence law of large numbers used below.  By the definition of maximal correlation, for square-integrable scalar variables \(U_i\) and \(U_j\) measurable with respect to the two unit sigma-fields,
\[
 |\operatorname{Cov}(U_i,U_j)|
 \leq\rho_{ij}\{\operatorname{Var}(U_i)\operatorname{Var}(U_j)\}^{1/2}.
\]
If \(\sup_i\mathbb E U_i^2\leq C\), then
\[
\operatorname{Var}\left(\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nU_i\right)
 \leq \frac{C}{n^2}\sum_{i,j=1}^n\rho_{ij}
 =O(n^{-q})=o(1).
\]
For every \(\eta>0\), the pointwise inequality \(\eta^2\mathbf 1\{|Z|>\eta\}\leq Z^2\), applied to the centered average \(Z\), implies that its tail probability is at most its variance divided by \(\eta^2\).  Thus \(n^{-1}\sum_i(U_i-\mathbb EU_i)=o_P(1)\).  Every design coordinate is bounded, and assumptions (ii)--(iii) give a uniform second-moment bound for every weighted design, outcome, or design--outcome coordinate used below.  Since \(T\) and \(d\) are fixed, the scalar conclusion holds jointly for all entries of the finitely many matrices and vectors.

Eliminating the unit intercepts in the weighted least-squares problem applies \(J\) to each unit's outcome and design.  Eliminating the centered time effect then subtracts the weighted cross-unit means.  Put
\[
 \widehat c_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\Theta_i,
 \qquad
 \widehat M_n=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n\Theta_iD_{W_i}}{\sum_{i=1}^n\Theta_i}.
\]
The preceding law of large numbers gives \(\widehat c_n=1+o_P(1)\) and \(\widehat M_n=M(\Pi)+o_P(1)\).  On the event \(\widehat c_n>0\), the coefficient normal equations are
\[
 \widehat G_n\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ex},n}=\widehat g_n,
\]
where
\[
 \widehat G_n=\frac1{nT}\sum_{i=1}^n\Theta_i
 (D_{W_i}-\widehat M_n)^{\top}J(D_{W_i}-\widehat M_n),
\]
\[
 \widehat g_n=\frac1{nT}\sum_{i=1}^n\Theta_i
 (D_{W_i}-\widehat M_n)^{\top}JY_i.
\]
Indeed these are exactly the Frisch--Waugh--Lovell equations after the two eliminations; the centering restrictions only choose representatives for the intercepts and do not alter the coefficient equation.

The law of large numbers and \(\widehat M_n-M(\Pi)=o_P(1)\) imply
\[
 \widehat G_n
 =\frac1{nT}\sum_{i=1}^n\Theta_i
 (D_{W_i}-M)^{\top}J(D_{W_i}-M)+o_P(1)
 =G(\Pi)+o_P(1).
\]
For the outcome moment, Cauchy--Schwarz, assumption (iii), and \(\widehat M_n-M=o_P(1)\) similarly give
\[
 \widehat g_n
 =\frac1{nT}\sum_{i=1}^n\Theta_i(D_{W_i}-M)^{\top}JY_i+o_P(1).
\]
Conditional inverse-propensity cancellation followed by assumption (iv) yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\mathbb E\!\left[\Theta_i(D_{W_i}-M)^{\top}JY_i\right]\\
 &\quad=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\Pi_s(D_s-M)^{\top}J\mathbb E[Y_i(s)]\\
 &\quad=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\Pi_s(D_s-M)^{\top}J\mu_i
 +\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{\ell=0}^p
 \left\{\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\Pi_s(D_s-M)^{\top}Je_t(D_s)_{t,\ell}\right\}\tau_{i,t,\ell}\\
 &\quad=T\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{\ell=0}^ph_{t,\ell}(\Pi)\tau_{i,t,\ell}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\mu_i=(\mu_{i1},\ldots,\mu_{iT})^{\top}\), and the baseline term is zero because \(\sum_s\Pi_s(D_s-M)=0\).  Applying the weak-dependence law of large numbers to the oracle outcome moment gives
\[
 \widehat g_n
 =\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{\ell=0}^p
 h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)\overline\tau_{t,\ell,n}+o_P(1).
\]

The deterministic vector on the right is bounded uniformly in \(n\): it equals \(T^{-1}n^{-1}\sum_i\sum_s\Pi_s(D_s-M)^{\top}J\mathbb E[Y_i(s)]\), whose norm is bounded by the finite design bound and assumption (iii).  Since \(G(\Pi)\succ0\), \(\widehat G_n\) is nonsingular with probability tending to one and \(\widehat G_n^{-1}=G(\Pi)^{-1}+o_P(1)\).  Multiplying the normal equation by this inverse proves
\[
 \widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ex},n}
 =\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{\ell=0}^p
 G(\Pi)^{-1}h_{t,\ell}(\Pi)\overline\tau_{t,\ell,n}+o_P(1),
\]
which is the first conclusion by the definition of \(L\).  Under calendar homogeneity, the normalization \(\sum_tL_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)=\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}\) from \(\mathrm{thm{:}calendar\text{-}lag\text{-}loading}\) reduces the \(j\)-th coordinate to \(n^{-1}\sum_i\tau_{i,j}+o_P(1)\), proving the last assertion.
added_lemmas.justification: This separates the design tensor from the i.i.d. superpopulation layer and carries it into the unit-indexed known-propensity framework used by the published dynamic RIPW theorem.
added_lemmas.gap: The published theorem treats calendar-homogeneous lag effects; the displayed limit gives the coefficient functional under unit-specific calendar-varying effects.
added_lemmas.consumer: Applied RIPW analyses can interpret the estimator with the same loading tensor under the published weak-dependence conditions.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every law in \(\mathcal M(T,p,\mathcal S,\epsilon)\), the reshaped fixed-effect coefficient satisfies
\[
 \theta(\Pi)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi)\tau_{t,\ell}.
\]
For arbitrary finite binary-path support, and \(j,r,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\),
\[
 G_{jr}(\Pi)=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}C_{\Pi}(t-j,t-r)
 -T^{-2}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{v=1}^{T}C_{\Pi}(t-j,v-r),
\]
\[
 h_{t,\ell,j}(\Pi)=T^{-1}\left\{C_{\Pi}(t-j,t-\ell)
 -T^{-1}\sum_{v=1}^{T}C_{\Pi}(v-j,t-\ell)\right\},
 \qquad
 \sum_{t=1}^{T}L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)=\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}.
\]
If \(\mathcal S\) is absorbing, then \(C_{\Pi}(u,v)=K_{\Pi}(u,v)\) on every argument used above, so the same two displays hold with \(K_{\Pi}\) in place of \(C_{\Pi}\).

The extension in outcome structure is strict: for \(T=3\), \(p=1\), \(\mathcal S=\{000,001,011\}\), and \(\Pi=(1/3,1/3,1/3)\),
\[

\]

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Suppose that \(\mathcal S\) is absorbing.  Order its distinct paths as \(\mathcal S=(s_1,\ldots,s_k)\) so that \(u_a=a(s_a)<u_b=a(s_b)\) when \(a<b\), and suppose \(\ker H_{\mathcal S}=\{0\}\).  For a fixed law with \(\Pi_{s_a}\geq\epsilon>0\), define \(\rho_a=\Pi_{s_{a+1}}/\Pi_{s_a}\), \(z_1=1\), \(z_a=\prod_{r=1}^{a-1}\rho_r\), and \(Z=\sum_{a=1}^kz_a\).  Let
\[
 (I_{ab})_{r,j}=\mathbf 1\{u_a\leq r-j<u_b\},
\]
\[
 \Gamma(\rho)=T^{-1}\sum_{a<b}z_az_bI_{ab}^{\top}JI_{ab},
 \qquad
 g_{t,\ell}(\rho)=T^{-1}\sum_{a<b}z_az_bI_{ab}^{\top}Je_t(I_{ab})_{t,\ell}.
\]
Then \(\det\Gamma(\rho)>0\).  If \(\Delta_{j,t,\ell}(\rho)\) is the determinant obtained by replacing column \(j\) of \(\Gamma(\rho)\) by \(g_{t,\ell}(\rho)\), then, for \(j,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\) and \(t\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\),
\[
 L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)=\frac{\Delta_{j,t,\ell}(\rho)}{\det\Gamma(\rho)},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{sgn}L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)=\operatorname{sgn}\Delta_{j,t,\ell}(\rho),
 \qquad
 L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)=0\Longleftrightarrow\Delta_{j,t,\ell}(\rho)=0.
\]
Consequently, at this fixed law all off-diagonal causal-lag loadings vanish if and only if \(\Delta_{j,t,\ell}(\rho)=0\) for all \(t\) and all \(j\neq\ell\).  The floor is equivalent to \(z_a\geq\epsilon Z\) for every \(a\).  On rationally represented endpoints and ratios, this is a terminating exact pointwise sign-and-zero certificate, including repeated or boundary-shifted coordinates.  It does not assert a global chamber classification as \(\rho\) varies.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Cramer's rule gives an exact certificate at a specified positive ratio vector, but it does not classify the determinant sign chambers over the entire feasible ratio region.  The proposed claim states exactly the pointwise result proved and fixes all malformed index ranges.

\[

\]
For arbitrary finite binary-path support, and \(j,r,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\),
\[

\]
\[

\]

proposed.comparator_claim: A conventional event-study lag coefficient is a weighted average of cohort effects from its own and other relative periods.
Inverse-probability estimators of finite-memory dynamic effects are unbiased under known panel randomization, with finite-population limit theory.
Under a time-constant random-coefficient distributed-lag model, average lag coefficients can be identified in complex treatment designs.
Conventional staggered event-study regressions admit computable probability-limit diagnostics for negative weights and cross-horizon contamination.
A time-varying parameter distributed-lag model permits lag coefficients to vary with past information.

prose_updates.tldr: For any finite binary-path support, the reshaped distributed-lag fixed-effect coefficient is an exact linear functional of calendar-by-lag effects, with Gram and loading numerators determined by the general path covariance \(C_{\Pi}\).  Absorbing supports add an ordered Green representation, a graph-theoretic full-rank criterion, and an exact pointwise Cramer sign certificate.  A separate theorem carries the tensor into the unit-indexed known-propensity and weak-dependence setup of Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo and recovers their homogeneous coefficient limit.  A global sign-chamber classification over all positive ratios remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published dynamic RIPW theory proves coefficient recovery for calendar-homogeneous effects under unit-specific known propensities and weakly dependent units, but does not give the calendar-specific loading tensor.  Existing event-study decompositions do not characterize counterfactual path-law reshaping for a finite-memory lag design.  Neither literature supplies an ordered combinatorial rank law or a global adjacent-ratio sign-chamber classification.
project_justification.niche: The missing objects are the support-general coefficient-by-calendar-by-causal-lag tensor, a design-only support-rank test, and, on absorbing supports, computable ordered endpoint certificates.
project_justification.fill: The note derives the tensor with the arbitrary-path covariance kernel \(C_{\Pi}\), recovers the ordered bridge kernel \(K_{\Pi}\) only under absorption, proves an absorbing-support graph criterion for full rank, supplies exact rational forward and pointwise sign certificates, and proves a calendar-varying estimator limit under the published unit-indexed sampling conditions.  It does not claim a global sign-chamber solution.

sampling_model.design: The design algebra fixes any finite support \(\mathcal S\subseteq\{0,1\}^{T}\) and an ex ante reshaping law \(\Pi\).  Absorption is imposed only for the adoption-order Green, graph, and adjacent-ratio corollaries.
sampling_model.units: The population identification layer uses a generic one-unit law \(P\) and supports i.i.d. sampling.  The anchor estimator theorem instead uses the published unit-indexed triangular array and permits non-i.i.d. weak dependence through \(n^{-2}\sum_{i,j}\rho_{ij}=O(n^{-q})\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment paths may be arbitrary binary vectors in the base algebra.  In the published-class theorem, \(\pi_i(w)=\mathbb P(W_i=w\mid\mathcal Y_i)\) is unit-specific and conditions on the full potential-outcome schedule; absorbing paths are a separate specialization.
sampling_model.overlap: The reshaping law satisfies \(\Pi_s\geq\epsilon\) on \(\mathcal S\).  The superpopulation layer assumes \(\pi_s(X)\geq c_{\pi}\), while the published-class theorem assumes \(\pi_i(s)\geq c_{\pi}\) for every reshaping-support path.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The population functional uses a generalized path propensity.  The published-class estimator corollary is proved for known unit-specific propensities, matching the anchor theorem; cross-fitted estimated-propensity or augmented full-path-mean inference is not established in this specialization.

prose_updates.related_work: Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo (2024) allow arbitrary treatment paths, unit-specific known propensities conditional on full potential-outcome schedules, and non-i.i.d. weakly dependent units.  The present superpopulation identification class is not their class: the two are incomparable overall, and the present class is narrower in its common-propensity and i.i.d. sampling interpretation.  The separate published-class calendar-loading theorem works directly under their Assumptions \(2.1\)--\(2.3\), extends the coefficient limit to unit- and calendar-specific lag effects, and gives their Theorem \(4.1\) conclusion under calendar homogeneity.  Sun and Abraham (2021) decompose conventional event-study coefficients rather than a reshaped finite-memory lag design.  Bojinov, Rambachan, and Shephard (2021) study finite-memory effects under known experimental assignment.  De Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2025) retain time-constant distributed-lag effects.  Wright (2026) supplies adjacent numerical event-study diagnostics but not assignment-law reshaping, and Ailigeng, Lu, and Wang (2023) provide modeling precedent for time-varying distributed-lag coefficients without the present causal panel geometry.
prose_updates.interpretation: The tensor \(L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)\) is a design-induced loading from the calendar \(t\), causal-lag \(\ell\) effect into regression coordinate \(j\); it is not itself a causal effect.  The equality for \(\theta(\Pi)\) follows from consistency, conditional mean assignment, and baseline cancellation.  For arbitrary paths the tensor is computed from \(C_{\Pi}\); adoption-order interpretations require absorption.  The graph criterion certifies whether all lag coordinates are estimable, while the determinant signs certify one specified reshaping law rather than an entire ratio chamber.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The pointwise determinant formula reduces each loading sign to an exact polynomial sign at a supplied adjacent-ratio vector, but no theorem classifies the connected sign chambers or all feasible determinant-zero frontiers over the continuous floor-constrained ratio region.  The note also does not solve the inverse image of a target tensor, certify a closest feasible loading with worst-case bounded-effect contamination, or establish cross-fitted augmented inference.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved scope consists of arbitrary-path pair-mass identities, a support-only kernel, the path-covariance loading formula and normalization, the absorbing Green corollary, an absorbing graph-rank criterion, exact rational forward diagnostics, a pointwise adjacent-ratio Cramer certificate, and a published-class estimator limit under known unit-specific propensities.  The superpopulation and published sampling classes are kept distinct; only the separate estimator theorem recovers the published homogeneous limit.  Global sign chambers, complete inverse membership, closest-loading optimization, worst-case bounded-effect contamination, and doubly robust cross-fitted inference remain outside the proved core.
